skill.name: Edit against a checklist
skill.why: A checklist shows exactly what a draft must do, so nothing gets missed.
skill.how: Take one checklist item at a time. Hunt the draft for proof it's done.

steps.say: Three checklist items. I check one at a time.

show.nudge: That's about when. Item 1 asks for the name of the game.
That's about where. Item 1 asks for the name of the game.

steps.ask: Item 1: Names the game. Tap the line that shows it.
steps.win: Yes! That line is the proof. Item 1 is done.

steps.say: Item 2: Gives the exact start time. Read it carefully.

check.nudge: Read item 2 again: exact start time. Could you set a clock by 'after lunch'?

steps.win: Right! After lunch isn't exact. Near enough still fails.

steps.say: I fix item 2, without breaking an item that passed.
steps.ask: Which edit fixes item 2 and keeps every other item?

options.text: Change 'after lunch' to 'soon after lunch'.
options.reason: Soon still isn't a clock time. Item 2 wants an exact time.

options.text: Change the first line to 'Come and play at 1.30 pm!'
options.reason: Now there is a time, but where did Lava Leap go? Item 1 breaks.

options.text: Change 'after lunch' to 'at 1.30 pm'.

steps.win: Yes! 1.30 pm is exact, and nothing else broke.

steps.say: Mo's checklist: each step starts with a command verb, like Mix.

show.nudge: Mix tells you what to do. That's a command verb, so it passes.
Stir tells you what to do, so it passes.

steps.ask: Tap the step that fails the item.
